title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct Rose Hill study settings, from reservable group rooms and research facilities to technology-rich workspaces and student lounges.

cards.title: Settle In Among the Stacks
cards.subtitle: Quiet research base at Rose Hill
cards.notes: Bring the assignment that needs sustained focus, then use the library’s collections, computer labs, and quieter study setting.
cards.short_summary: A collection-rich home base for individual research and focused reading.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies Walsh Library as a quiet place to research or study and says it contains more than one million volumes and four computer labs.
cards.source_title: Commuter Campus Hangouts at Rose Hill
cards.access_notes: Use during posted library hours, which vary by academic session; consult Fordham Libraries for current hours.

cards.title: Book a First-Floor Team Room
cards.subtitle: Reservable room for two to four students
cards.notes: Create your reservation account before the project crunch, then bring a two-to-four-person group for focused collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A clearly mapped first-floor room for small-group research sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s Walsh Library map identifies Room 116 as a first-floor group study room; library policy designates all Walsh study rooms for groups of two to four students.
cards.access_notes: Current undergraduate and graduate students may reserve it through Booked Scheduler for up to two hours per 24-hour period.

cards.entity_name: Walsh Library Archives and Special Collections Research Room
cards.title: Work Directly With Primary Sources
cards.subtitle: Fourth-floor supervised research space
cards.notes: Check the finding aids first, store prohibited belongings in the lockers, and arrive ready to work with a laptop and pencil.
cards.short_summary: A controlled research setting for careful work with rare and archival material.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham states that Archives and Special Collections has on-site research rooms on Walsh Library’s fourth floor and permits only laptops and pencils in the research room.
cards.access_notes: Open to the Fordham community and research scholars, Monday through Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; materials do not circulate.

cards.title: Build the Multimedia Version
cards.subtitle: Walsh Library Lower Level, Room 014
cards.notes: Bring a project that benefits from shared screens or fabrication, and match your work session to the center’s weekday schedule.
cards.short_summary: A technology-forward collaboration space for making, recording, and prototyping.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says Rose Hill students have access to LITE Center collaboration areas with lounges, TVs, and Jamboards, plus recording, XR, and makerspace facilities.
cards.access_notes: Located in Walsh Library, Lower Level, Room 014; Fordham lists hours as Monday–Thursday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Take a Gallery Table
cards.subtitle: Open work setting inside the campus center
cards.notes: Choose this visible, open setting for laptop work between commitments, especially when complete silence is not essential.
cards.short_summary: An airy campus-center setting suited to a short reading or writing block.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham’s McShane Center page identifies the First Floor Gallery and depicts a student studying at one of its tables.
cards.access_notes: An open first-floor campus-center space; check campus-center operations and event activity before relying on a quiet setting.

cards.title: Read From a Sectional
cards.subtitle: Soft seating in the McShane Center
cards.notes: Use the sectional seating for lighter reading, review, or planning that does not require a desk-sized work surface.
cards.short_summary: A softer alternative for reading and low-equipment coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies the Simpson Family Lounge by name and documents sectional couches in its McShane Center lounge area.
cards.access_notes: Located in the McShane Center; it is a shared lounge, so seating and noise conditions may change with campus activity.

cards.title: Spread Out at the Square Table
cards.subtitle: First-floor table seating with nearby amenities
cards.notes: Bring group notes or a larger laptop setup to the square table, while expecting the normal movement of a student-center lounge.
cards.short_summary: A table-based option for collaborative work in the center of campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham identifies the Student Lounge on McShane Center’s first floor and documents students studying at a large square table near the lounge area.
cards.access_notes: This is a shared first-floor lounge rather than a reservable quiet room; availability can vary around programs and meals.

cards.title: Move the Work Session Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Between-class lounge near student offices
cards.notes: Use this upstairs lounge for a work block between classes, with student-involvement and commuter offices close at hand.
cards.short_summary: A practical upstairs landing place for independent work between meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham describes the McShane Center Second Floor Lounge as a place to work or relax between classes and locates student-organization offices on the same floor.
cards.source_title: Commuter Campus Hangouts at Rose Hill
cards.access_notes: Shared campus-center lounge near the Office for Student Involvement and Commuting Students Association offices.

cards.title: Bring the Team to the Booths
cards.subtitle: Business-school lounge with iMacs and tables
cards.notes: Choose the booth-style tables for team planning, or use the lounge’s iMacs when your own device is not the right tool.
cards.short_summary: A business-school collaboration setting with computers and booth-style tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham says the Hughes Hall student lounge contains iMacs, large flat-screen televisions, and restaurant-booth-style tables suited to team meetings.
cards.access_notes: Inside the Gabelli School’s Rose Hill building; confirm building access when visiting outside normal class activity.

cards.title: Use the Honors Home Base
cards.subtitle: Computers and printers for Honors students
cards.notes: If you are in the Honors Program, use the basement for a study session and keep the on-site computers and printers in mind.
cards.short_summary: A restricted-access Honors workspace equipped for both discussion and production.
cards.evidence_claim: Fordham documents the Alpha House basement lounge as a study-session space equipped with computers and printers for Honors student use.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to Honors Program students; Fordham states that all Honors students receive 24/7 Alpha House access.
